lyrics:
[Intro: bouncing bass line, handclaps, a drum fill]

[Verse 1: male tenor, flustered and eager]
I've got a tie I haven't worn since the wedding
And a heart that's doing things it shouldn't do
You walked in wearing red like you were betting
And my blood pressure's blaming you

[Verse 2: female soprano, cool and in charge]
Straighten up that collar, mister, find your nerve
I didn't do my hair to stand around
There's a slow one and a fast one, I'll take both
So put that glass of water down

[Chorus: both voices, full band, handclaps]
Look at you (look at me)
Look at us, ooh, ooh, ooh
Forty years and I'd still pick you
Out of any room, ooh, ooh, ooh
Look at you (look at me)
Still my kind of trouble

[Verse 3: male then female, trading lines]
If my knees give out, you'll have to catch me
(If your knees give out, I'll leave you where you fall)
I've been practising my spin out in the garage
(I know, I saw you from the hall)

[Chorus: both voices, full band, handclaps]
Look at you (look at me)
Look at us, ooh, ooh, ooh
Forty years and I'd still pick you
Out of any room, ooh, ooh, ooh
Look at you (look at me)
Still my kind of trouble

[Bridge: band drops to bass and claps, voices close]
Ooh, ooh, ooh
(Is that the tie?) It's the tie
Ooh, ooh, ooh
(Come here)

[Final Chorus: everything, saxophone on top, whoops]
Look at you (look at me)
Look at us, ooh, ooh, ooh
Forty years and I'd still pick you
Out of any room, ooh, ooh, ooh
Look at you (look at me)
Still my kind of trouble

[Outro: bass line, laughing, last shout]
Look at us
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 107 BPM, 4/4, C major. A bouncing, strutting pop-rock groove. Flirtatious, bright and theatrical.

VOICE: A man with a light, eager tenor that cracks into falsetto when he is flustered. A woman with a bright, clear soprano and a teasing edge who sounds entirely in control. They trade lines quickly and sing the chorus together, with a wordless three-note 'ooh' hook.

INSTRUMENTS: A bouncing, repeating electric bass line that drives the song. A tight drum kit with a strong backbeat. Handclaps. Rhythm guitar. Piano. A tenor saxophone in the last chorus. A few synthesised string stabs in the chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the bass line, claps and a fill. 0:09 Verse 1, the man. 0:27 Verse 2, the woman. 0:45 Chorus 1. 1:07 Verse 3, traded lines. 1:25 Chorus 2. 1:47 Bridge, bass and claps with spoken asides. 2:05 Final chorus with saxophone. 2:30 Outro, the bass line, laughter and a shout at 2:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1970s film-musical pop: bright, punchy and clean, the two voices upfront and dry, the band tight.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first shared 'ooh, ooh, ooh' in the chorus at 0:50.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original pair are teenagers who change themselves to match. These two have forty years behind them, bad knees and a garage, and the joke is that they can still surprise each other.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fluster, teasing, delight.
